topic: Grade XI Physics Unit 7.3 Elastic Potential Energy
officialFramework: FBISE Physics Grade XI Assessment Framework, Curriculum 2022-23, Scheme of Studies 2024
rowFingerprintMethod: SHA-256 over UTF-8 JSON of exact Word cell strings trimmed on both ends; keys 'stem','options','keyLetter','correctOptionText','oneLineExplanation','slo','level'; JSON sorted keys, ensure_ascii=false, separators comma/colon; original question number excluded.

sourceBookGraphAxesKnownDiscrepancy.formula: W = integral F dx; triangular 0.5*F*x only for linear loading from zero

crossBatchBlueprintNote: P-11-B-27 and P-11-B-28 are official Summative/Application SLOs, but none of their original Q1–20 items is tagged Application; review Q21–80 for genuine application tasks before whole-bank claims. Two items tagged A under B-25 are recognitional and require a teacher cognitive decision.

sourceBoundItems.issue: Original Q3 asks what NBF Figure 7.13 illustrates but provides no actual diagram or equivalent apparatus description. A standalone portal question must supply its own information instead of relying on an unavailable textbook illustration.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Retain the owner original privately; attach an original/authorized reference-wire/vernier apparatus figure with text alternative or rewrite into a self-contained experiment scenario, then re-QC the item.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Original can remain as textbook-dependent revision; use a separately source-bound self-contained candidate for scored student use.

sourceBoundItems.issue: The hanging-mass force relationship is physically valid, but several distractors are dimensionally implausible; another question in this batch tests the same relationship with almost identical reasoning.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Keep the source original, improve distractor plausibility if preparing a new scored variant and compare with Q18 before placing both in one randomized test.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Yes, the original remains useful as quick study recall; do not automatically publish both near-duplicates together.

sourceBoundItems.issue: Original Q6 is labelled Application but currently asks students to recognize the algebraic Young's-modulus formula. No numerical data, unfamiliar experimental situation or formula derivation is required; official P-11-B-25 is Summative Understanding.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Preserve the correct original choice. Reclassify its actual item demand as Understanding for a reviewed copy, or construct a genuine application scenario separately; never relabel an unchanged recognition question as A without justification.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Keep the original formula-recognition question; an additional real apparatus/numerical item can be created if application depth is needed.

sourceBoundItems.issue: The question uses the scientifically correct force-vertical/extension-horizontal graph convention for work as area. However, original NBF Figure 7.14 on p.122 places weight on the horizontal axis and extension vertically, which can mislead students relying on the printed figure.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Keep the scientifically correct key; in the scored teaching context explicitly define graph axes and explain the textbook's reversed convention. If a graph is shown, use original source-checked force-versus-extension axes and accessible labels.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Yes, original is scientifically valid; pair with clear graph-axis notes or a revised self-contained stimulus rather than changing the correct physical answer.

sourceBoundItems.issue: The source wording 'elastic loading from rest' does not by itself guarantee that applied force rises linearly from zero. The average force equals half the final force only for linear proportional loading over the interval.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Use 'loading from zero force to final F within the proportional elastic range' or an equivalent explicit straight-line force-extension condition in the future scored stem.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Retain the original archival question with the correct key; publish a separately checked clarified version for standalone assessment.

sourceBoundItems.issue: Original Q13 asks for the synonym of elastic potential energy, following Q1's recall of the energy name. Both are scientifically valid but close in the underlying knowledge tested.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Retain both for vocabulary practice; if a short scored paper needs greater diversity, prefer one recall item and introduce a conceptual energy transfer or area-under-graph question instead.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Yes, both source-valid items can remain in the study bank; the final teacher will decide random-test sampling.

sourceBoundItems.issue: The stiffness/gradient fact is correct for a straight graph with force on the vertical axis and extension on the horizontal. NBF Figure 7.14 reverses those axes; future reuse should avoid ambiguity about which slope is meant.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Clarify 'gradient of force F plotted vertically against extension x horizontally' or provide an original labelled graph in the future scored version.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Keep original in the private bank, with a clearer graph label when taught beside the textbook figure.

sourceBoundItems.issue: Q18 substantially repeats Q5's physical relationship for a stationary hanging mass with almost no different reasoning demand. Both original answer choices are correct, but using both together adds little assessment diversity.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Keep both original source questions but avoid scheduling both as distinct exam-evidence items; replace one with a reference-wire calibration or changing-load experiment scenario if needed.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Yes, keep the original in an archival or quick-revision pool; decide which one will appear in each scored set after teacher approval.

sourceBoundItems.issue: Q19 is labelled Application but selects the cross-sectional-area formula for wire diameter, which primarily assesses a prerequisite geometry identity, not an experimental application. The explicit circular-area substitution appears in the textbook's worked calculation on p.124 even though the source answer cites p.123.
sourceBoundItems.proposedAction: Retain the correct geometry relation, fix the cited detailed formula context to p.124 or distinguish the general p.122 area measurement, and classify as supporting experimental knowledge unless embedded in a wire-modulus calculation.
sourceBoundItems.originalCanBeKept: Keep the original source item as prerequisite study; use an actual measured diameter/force/extension calculation for scored application evidence.
